newsitem.title: USA: FIGURE SKATING-OLYMPIC CHAMPION BAIUL ARRESTED FOR DRUNK DRIVING.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-OLYMPIC CHAMPION BAIUL ARRESTED FOR DRUNK DRIVING.

text.p: Olympic figure skating champion Oksana Baiul Tuesday turned herself into police and was arrested on charges of drunken and reckless driving after she ran her car off a road during a weekend accident.

"Today at approximately four p.m., Oksana Baiul came voluntarily to the Bloomfield Police Department, was arrested by warrant for reckless driving and driving under the influence of alcohol," a Bloomfield Police spokesman said.
The 19-year-old Baiul, darling of the 1994 Lillehammer Winter Games for her gold medal performance, was released on a written promise to appear in court on January 27, police said.

Local news reports have said hospital documents showed the Ukrainian, who now lives and trains in the Hartford suburb of Simsbury, had a blood-alcohol level of .168 percent, well above Connecticut's legal limit of .10.
Baiul is also two years younger than Connecticut's legal drinking age of 21.

Baiul suffered a concussion and bad cut on the back of her head which required 14 stitches early Sunday after losing control of her car, leaving skid marks more than 100 feet (30 m) long. She veered off a road into some trees in the Hartford suburb of Bloomfield.

Baiul was discharged from St. Francis Hospital and Medical Centre in Hartford early Monday morning after being held overnight for observation. A passenger in Baiul's car was treated for a broken finger and released.
"Health-wise she's much better, she's up and around," Bob Young, director of the International Skating Centre and a friend of Baiul, told Reuters.
"She's healing fine, and with two to three weeks of rest she'll be 100 percent back to normal.
"Mentally, she knows she's made a pretty major mistake, and she's going to pay some consequences for it," Young said.

Baiul, a national hero in Ukraine after winning the nation's first Olympic gold medal, has trained at the International Skating Centre in Simsbury for the past two years because of poor training conditions back home.
